---
title: "experiment tracking"
---

## what is a run?

- a run is one execution with a particular dataset, configuration, and environment
- tracking connects the choices you made to the outputs they produced
- keep failed runs too, with their status and logs, so failures can be investigated

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| record | examples |
|---|---|
| inputs | dataset snapshot, feature list, split ids |
| code | git commit and whether there were uncommitted changes |
| settings | hyperparameters, seed, preprocessing choices |
| environment | dependency versions, container digest, hardware |
| results | validation metrics, runtime, warnings |
| artifacts | fitted pipeline, predictions, evaluation report |

:::

## compare like with like

- use the same dataset version, split, metric definition, and evaluation procedure
- change one factor at a time initially so differences are easier to interpret
- inspect variation across seeds or folds rather than relying on one favourable score
- use validation results to choose candidates; keep the final test set out of the tuning loop

## add mlflow to the lifecycle example

- install `mlflow` in your project environment, then run this from the folder containing `artifacts/run-001`
- it records the results already produced by the [lifecycle example](../foundations/lifecycle.qmd), without inventing new scores
- mlflow organises runs and logs parameters, metrics, tags, and artifacts [tracking guide](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/ml/tracking/)

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path
import mlflow

report = json.loads(Path("artifacts/run-001/run.json").read_text())
mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///mlflow.db")
mlflow.set_experiment("lifecycle-demo")
with mlflow.start_run():
    mlflow.log_params({"c": report["selected_c"], "seed": report["seed"]})
    mlflow.log_metric("validation_auc", report["selected_validation_auc"])
    mlflow.set_tag("data_sha256", report["data_sha256"])
    mlflow.log_artifacts("artifacts/run-001", artifact_path="run-output")
```

- save the git commit, split identifiers, and dependency lock file alongside the run too
- a data fingerprint identifies bytes, but does not preserve the dataset itself
- logging a joblib file as an artifact does not create an mlflow model or register it automatically

## connect research workflow records

- nextflow reports and task traces capture execution details; attach them to the corresponding experiment [nextflow reports](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reports)
- record the container digest and slurm job ids alongside the workflow run id
- execution records explain how a pipeline ran; you still need task-specific metrics to judge its results
